Meanwhile ANZ Investment Bank said it had been mandated to lead a three-year Eurobond issue for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The deal will be roadshowed in mid-March and launch is expected before the end of March.
ANZ new issues syndicate official Jo Cunningham said further details of the Eurobond were not yet finalised but that it would be a benchmark dollar transaction for the borrower.

In December 1994 Pakistan launched a $150 million 11.50 percent December 1999 bond. It was launched to yield 385 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and was last trading at 415 b.p. over. Pakistan is rated B2 by Moody's and B+ by S&P.
The rand sector saw a total of 800 million rand raised on Thursday by the International Finance Corp, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Helaba Finance and a unit of Volkswagen.
The IFC launched the longest-dated Eurorand bond, which is also the first ever zero-coupon Eurorand issue.

Gerry Moes, syndicate manager at lead manager Hambros Bank, a regular underwriter in the Eurorand sector, said it was a ground-breaking transaction. The 500 million rand zero-coupon 10-year bond yields just over 14.0 percent.
